scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

structural_remedies.description: Audit the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) to determine whether any rule changes occurred between July and September.
structural_remedies.rationale: Log review can be completed well within the remaining 225 minutes; no protected actions are involved.; residual gap: If no rule changes are found, the root cause remains unknown and other factors must be investigated; if changes are found, the gap is closed only after faulty rules are reverted or corrected.

structural_remedies.description: If the audit confirms faulty validation rules, revert those rules to the pre‑July version (or a known‑good version).
structural_remedies.rationale: Reverting a configuration change is a manual admin action that does not write to customer bills, thus respects K-BILLWRITE; it can be done quickly once the offending rule set is identified.; residual gap: Assuming the faulty rules are the sole source of calculation errors, the gap is eliminated; any additional error sources would leave a residual gap.

structural_remedies.description: Introduce a change‑control workflow for billing import validation rule modifications (requiring Billing Operations approval and an audit trail) to prevent future erroneous rule changes.
structural_remedies.rationale: Defining and documenting the workflow is a planning activity that does not trigger any protected actions and fits within the time budget.; residual gap: This prevents recurrence but does not correct existing incorrect bills, so a residual gap remains until current bills are fixed.

proposal.summary: The problem is that recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced calculation errors that produce incorrect bills even when actual reads are present, driving the observed increase in dispute tickets. This was established by evidence showing dispute volume rise (E-03), more disputed bills with actual than estimated reads (E-01), and a large number of disputed estimated bills having AMI reads rejected due to high consumption (E-11), indicating rule changes are rejecting valid reads. The release attempted to validate bill calculation using accounts estimated last cycle, notify affected customers, and update dispute response templates. The decision is HOLD because the release assumes completeness of DA-RULES while its completeness is unknown, and the safety predicate/verification was not established (Layer 1 failed). Known limitations include the conditional pass gate with deferred items tracked as VOBs and an open VOB-U-U1 whose blocking scope lies outside the release scope. Evidence cited: E-01, E-03, E-11.
